name: asuswrt
description: Inspect and control an ASUS (AsusWRT) home router: connected devices, WAN, firewall, port forwarding, guest WiFi and WiFi security.
long_description:
Talks to the router's HTTP API — the same one the official ASUS mobile app uses. No SSH and no web-UI scraping.

This bundle is the wiring, not the server: install the server first with `uv tool install "asuswrt[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/gittycat/asuswrt-tools"`, and put the router's admin password in `~/.config/asuswrt/.env`. The password is read on this machine only and is never sent to a model.

The extension is read-only until you turn on "Allow changes to the router". Even then, every change is returned as a preview first and applied only on a second, confirmed call.

Two router settings this extension will not suggest turning on: AiProtection (and Traffic Analyzer, Adaptive QoS, Web History), because they are all gated behind one Trend Micro EULA that sends browsing data off the router; and DoS protection, because it only rate-limits traffic to roughly one packet per second, which breaks legitimate connections without stopping a real flood. Both reading as off is the expected state, not a problem to fix.

server_path.title: Path to asuswrt-mcp
server_path.description: Where uv put the server. Leave as it is unless you installed it somewhere else.

allow_writes.title: Allow changes to the router
allow_writes.description: Off: Claude can only read the router. On: it can also add port forwards, switch guest WiFi on or off, and change WiFi security — always showing a preview and asking before it applies anything.

allow_dangerous.title: Allow reboot and firmware upgrade
allow_dangerous.description: Needs the setting above as well. Adds two tools that restart the router or flash new firmware.

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Broad status in one call: identity, health, WAN and client counts

tools.name: get_system
tools.description: Model, firmware version, MAC and AiMesh role

tools.name: get_health
tools.description: Uptime, CPU per core, RAM and WAN link state

tools.name: get_wan
tools.description: Internet connection: link state, IP, gateway, DNS, protocol

tools.name: get_dns
tools.description: WAN resolvers, and what LAN clients are told to use

tools.name: get_led
tools.description: Whether the router's status lights are on

tools.name: get_upnp
tools.description: Whether devices can open their own inbound ports

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: Connected and known devices with name, vendor, IP and connection type

tools.name: get_firewall_and_filters
tools.description: Firewall, DoS protection, WAN admin access, URL and keyword filters

tools.name: get_parental_control
tools.description: Parental control state and its rules

tools.name: list_port_forwards
tools.description: Port forwarding rules, and whether forwarding is on at all

tools.name: list_guest_networks
tools.description: Guest wireless networks per band, with SSID and state

tools.name: get_wireless
tools.description: WPS, WPA mode, management frame protection and country code

tools.name: check_firmware_update
tools.description: Ask the router to check ASUS for a newer firmware, with release notes

tools.name: get_nvram
tools.description: Read raw router settings by name (read-only; there is no raw write)

tools.name: add_port_forward
tools.description: Forward an external port to a device on the LAN

tools.name: remove_port_forward
tools.description: Remove port forwarding rules by name and/or external port

tools.name: set_port_forwarding_enabled
tools.description: Turn port forwarding on or off globally, keeping the rules

tools.name: set_parental_control_enabled
tools.description: Turn parental control on or off

tools.name: set_guest_network_enabled
tools.description: Turn one guest wireless network on or off

tools.name: set_wps_enabled
tools.description: Turn Wi-Fi Protected Setup on or off on both bands

tools.name: set_wifi_security
tools.description: Set the WPA mode and 802.11w management frame protection

tools.name: set_wifi_country
tools.description: Set the regulatory country code

tools.name: set_wan_dns
tools.description: Set the WAN DNS servers, or hand them back to the ISP

tools.name: set_led_enabled
tools.description: Turn the router's status lights on or off

tools.name: set_upnp_enabled
tools.description: Turn UPnP on or off; off is the safe state

tools.name: reboot_router
tools.description: Reboot the router, dropping every connection in the house

tools.name: upgrade_firmware
tools.description: Download and flash a named firmware version
